subject: Culture
title: The Business Suit
description: A 60-second lesson on The Business Suit.

hook.text: The modern suit descends from 17th-century English court dress. King Charles II simplified it after the Great Fire.

buildup.text: The suit became democracy's uniform. It replaced aristocratic finery with a standardized male silhouette.

discovery.text: Beau Brummell in the 1810s defined modern men's fashion: dark colors, clean lines, and perfect fit over ornament.

twist.text: Silicon Valley's hoodie culture was a deliberate rejection of the suit—casual dress as a power move.

climax.text: In Japan, 'Cool Biz' campaigns let workers ditch jackets in summer, saving billions in air-conditioning costs.

punchline.text: The suit proved that restraint can be more powerful than display.

quiz.question: Who defined the modern aesthetic of the men's suit?

details.summary: The business suit — born from 17th-century English aristocracy — became the global uniform of power, professionalism, and masculinity. Its uniformity masks individual identity behind a shared code that signals competence, authority, and conformity to corporate culture.
details.whyItMatters: The suit's global dominance reveals how Western business culture exported its dress code worldwide. Understanding the suit means understanding how clothing enforces professional hierarchies.
takeaways: The modern suit evolved from 17th-century English court dress
Suits became the global standard for professional authority
The silicon valley hoodie challenges suit-based power signals

faq.question: Why did the suit become the standard for business?
faq.answer: The suit evolved from the matching coat-waistcoat-trousers ensemble popularized by England's Charles II. Industrial capitalism spread it as a symbol of rationality and seriousness. Its uniformity signaled reliability and professionalism, making it the default for anyone seeking business credibility.

faq.question: Is the business suit declining?
faq.answer: Yes, in many sectors. Tech culture's casual dress code and remote work have eroded suit dominance. However, suits remain standard in law, finance, and politics. The COVID-19 pandemic accelerated casual dress acceptance, with many companies permanently relaxing dress codes.
